In Zero Trust: Access controls → Access settings → Set your global session duration → Edit → 1 month → Save (docs/deploy/cloudflare.md step 3)

If it is lost, rotate it: Zero Trust → Access controls → Service credentials → Service Tokens → dashboard-backups-host → Rotate
  create      Access application                   Officer Dashboard

  create      Access application                   Officer Dashboard: services (service token)
  ok          Access application                   Dashboard backups (service token)  [app-backups]
                                                     - named "Backup sink" (matched by hostname and paths)
  create      Rule (http_request_firewall_custom)  Agents and services: skip bot checks
                                                     - the zone has no http_request_firewall_custom ruleset yet; the first write creates it
  create      Rule (http_request_cache_settings)   Agents and services: bypass cache
                                                     - the zone has no http_request_cache_settings ruleset yet; the first write creates it
  create      Rule (http_config_settings)          Consent page: no rewriting
                                                     - the zone has no http_config_settings ruleset yet; the first write creates it
  drift       Bot Fight Mode                       off
                                                     - Bot Fight Mode is on for the whole zone; agents cannot pass its challenges (docs/deploy/cloudflare.md step 6.1)
  ok          D1 database                          dashboard-backups  [d1-backups]
  drift       D1 migrations                        dashboard-backups
                                                     - found tables budgets, chunks, d1_migrations, snapshots; expected the Worker's schema, but it lacks the Worker's shape (table budgets is defined as "create table budgets(day text primary key,writes integer)"; the Worker's migration defines it as "create table budgets(day text primary key,writes integer not null default 0,uploads integer not null default 0)"). Setup never alters a database that already has tables, so it cannot lose data
                                                     - What to do: if the database holds no backups yet, delete it in the dashboard (Workers & Pages → D1 → dashboard-backups → Settings) and run setup again; otherwise compare it with server/deploy/backup-sink/migrations and create what is missing with `npx wrangler d1 execute dashboard-backups --remote --command "…"`, then record each migration with INSERT INTO d1_migrations (name) VALUES ('<file name>'). Or: leave it and start a separate install beside it with --name-prefix and its own hostname, which makes a fresh database.
  drift       Worker                               dashboard-backup-sink  [dashboard-backup-sink]
                                                     - found BACKUPS bound to D1 database d1-old; expected dashboard-backups (d1-backups)
                                                     - found compatibility date 2025-01-01; expected 2026-07-30
                                                     - What to do: setup never changes an existing Worker, because an upload replaces its whole script, bindings and secrets. Redeploy it with Wrangler from this release's server/deploy/backup-sink, whose wrangler.toml holds the expected settings (docs/deploy/fresh-install.md step 4); or delete it in the dashboard (Workers & Pages → dashboard-backup-sink → Settings → Delete) and run setup again, which uploads it as expected with the bearer in secrets/backup/bearer; or leave it and start a separate install beside it with --name-prefix and its own hostname.
  unknowable  Worker version                       revision 2
                                                     - Cloudflare shows no SINK_REVISION binding on it (it was deployed with Wrangler, or before this version of setup), so its revision is not known here
                                                     - What to do: nothing, unless you want setup to see the revision: backups keep working, and the backup service alerts if the Worker is ever too old for it. To label it, redeploy it with Wrangler adding --var SINK_REVISION:2.
  ok          workers.dev and preview URLs         off
  unknowable  Worker secret                        BACKUP_BEARER_SECRET
                                                     - set, but Cloudflare never returns its value, and the preview cannot see the host's secret files
                                                     - What to do: nothing while backups work. If the backup service is refused (401), the Worker's value is not the one in secrets/backup/bearer: set it with `npx wrangler secret put BACKUP_BEARER_SECRET` in server/deploy/backup-sink and paste that file's value (docs/deploy/fresh-install.md step 4.5).
  ok          Worker custom domain                 backups.example.org  [wd-1]

11 ok, 10 create, 3 drift, 3 unknowable, 1 manual

Cloudflare apply plan for officers.example.org

  WARNING: officers.example.org is already published (tunnel route or DNS record exists) but no Access application protects it. Setup changes nothing that publishes the hostname, and creates its Access application at step 5; the hostname stays unprotected until that step reads back ok. Do not start cloudflared until this run reports done.

   1. add the One-time PIN identity provider
   2. create Access group Officers
   3. create Access group Launchpad
   4. create service token officer-dashboard services
   5. create Access application Officer Dashboard with policy Officers and Launchpad
   6. create Access application Officer Dashboard: agents (bypass) with policy Everyone (bypass)
   7. create Access application Officer Dashboard: services (service token) with policy Service token
   8. add rule "Agents and services: skip bot checks" to http_request_firewall_custom (create the phase's ruleset with it)
   9. add rule "Agents and services: bypass cache" to http_request_cache_settings (create the phase's ruleset with it)
  10. add rule "Consent page: no rewriting" to http_config_settings (create the phase's ruleset with it)
  11. fetch the token of tunnel 6ff42ae2-765d-4adf-8112-31c55c1551ef (the host has none)
  manual: Bot Fight Mode is on for the whole zone. Setup leaves it, because it also affects the zone's other hostnames. In the Cloudflare dashboard, open the domain → Security → Settings → filter Bot traffic → Bot Fight Mode → Off (docs/deploy/cloudflare.md step 6.1)
  manual: the zone has 1 rate limiting rules. docs/deploy/cloudflare.md step 6.2 says the skip rule should also tick "All rate limiting rules" if you have them. In the domain: Security → Security rules → Agents and services: skip bot checks → Edit → tick All rate limiting rules → Save
  manual: Global session duration 730h (1 month) (not set (Cloudflare's default is 24h). Setup does not write the Zero Trust organization unless allowed. In Zero Trust: Access controls → Access settings → Set your global session duration → Edit → 1 month → Save (docs/deploy/cloudflare.md step 3))
  manual: the host has no client secret for service token dashboard-backups-host in secrets/backup/access-client-secret; if it is lost, rotate it: Zero Trust → Access controls → Service credentials → Service Tokens → dashboard-backups-host → Rotate, then write the new secret and its Client ID to secrets/backup/access-client-secret and secrets/backup/access-client-id (owner 10001, mode 0400)

Needs your attention (10):
  - manual: Bot Fight Mode is on for the whole zone. Setup leaves it, because it also affects the zone's other hostnames. In the Cloudflare dashboard, open the domain → Security → Settings → filter Bot traffic → Bot Fight Mode → Off (docs/deploy/cloudflare.md step 6.1)
  - manual: the zone has 1 rate limiting rules. docs/deploy/cloudflare.md step 6.2 says the skip rule should also tick "All rate limiting rules" if you have them. In the domain: Security → Security rules → Agents and services: skip bot checks → Edit → tick All rate limiting rules → Save
  - manual: Global session duration 730h (1 month) (not set (Cloudflare's default is 24h). Setup does not write the Zero Trust organization unless allowed. In Zero Trust: Access controls → Access settings → Set your global session duration → Edit → 1 month → Save (docs/deploy/cloudflare.md step 3))
  - manual: the host has no client secret for service token dashboard-backups-host in secrets/backup/access-client-secret; if it is lost, rotate it: Zero Trust → Access controls → Service credentials → Service Tokens → dashboard-backups-host → Rotate, then write the new secret and its Client ID to secrets/backup/access-client-secret and secrets/backup/access-client-id (owner 10001, mode 0400)

If it is lost, rotate it: Zero Trust → Access controls → Service credentials → Service Tokens → dashboard-backups-host → Rotate

Setup never alters a database that already has tables, so it cannot lose data
      What to do: if the database holds no backups yet, delete it in the dashboard (Workers & Pages → D1 → dashboard-backups → Settings) and run setup again; otherwise compare it with server/deploy/backup-sink/migrations and create what is missing with `npx wrangler d1 execute dashboard-backups --remote --command "…"`, then record each migration with INSERT INTO d1_migrations (name) VALUES ('<file name>').       What to do: setup never changes an existing Worker, because an upload replaces its whole script, bindings and secrets.
